text:
maria: Heads up — after the kernel rollout in us-west1, the ephemeral cleaner started marking a big batch of blocks as PRESERVE. ~4.2k extents flagged, and we're seeing GPU attach stalls in that region.

josh: ugh. how long ago did the rollout finish?

maria: ~35m ago. deploy-bot reported success, then ops-bot started spamming warnings about attach latency.

ops-bot: [alert] region=us-west1 service=ephemeral-cleaner severity=warning msg=preserve-flag-surge count=4217

josh: can you paste the cleaner log tail?

maria: sure — snippet below. looks like a regression in the new free-space scanner path.

```
2026-03-23T10:12:07Z cleaner: scan complete bucket=hotwalk flagged=21
2026-03-23T10:12:18Z cleaner: scan complete bucket=warmwalk flagged=198
2026-03-23T10:12:26Z cleaner: preserve-mark apply start range=(0x7f..0x9b) reason=kernel-fixpath
2026-03-23T10:12:26Z cleaner: preserve-mark applied count=4217 duration=0.12s
2026-03-23T10:12:27Z attach-provisioner: attach_wait avg_ms=4300 95p=12s
```

tess: that `preserve-mark` path wasn't supposed to be enabled by default — it was gated behind `--preserve-experimental` in the patch. maybe the flag didn't gate correctly. :eyes:

samir: if those blocks are flagged preserve, janitor won't reclaim into the hot pool. that can starve GPU attach for workloads needing scratch. we should either revert the kernel change or flip the cleaner config to opt-out.

maria: I'm leaning to flip cleaner config and trigger a targeted `unpreserve` pass. revert will take longer (infra rollout).

josh: agree. short term: disable the new scanner and run `cleaner unpreserve --region us-west1 --reason=rollback-flagging --max=5000`? we need to avoid O(N) overloading the NVMe. add rate limit.

maria: running throttle cmd now: `rvctl svc config set ephemeral-cleaner --region us-west1 --preserve-mode=off --apply-immediately`

ops-bot: [info] config-change queued by maria for ephemeral-cleaner/us-west1

nora-support: support is seeing a spike in customer-reported attach timeouts for Dedicated customers in us-west1. I'm sending a banner to affected tenants now and routing to success.

samir: once we flip, we should run a conservative repair: `cleaner unpreserve --region us-west1 --batch=200 --sleep-ms=250` and watch nvme_iops and attach-queue depth.

josh: also propose we temporarily throttle job scheduler to avoid mass GPU launch storms while we unpreserve. set `scheduler.max-attach-concurrent=100` for the region. that buys us headroom.

maria: done — scheduler knob lowered. starting unpreserve in 2m. will stream logs to this thread. :thumbsup:

(2m later)

maria: unpreserve started. first batch returned ~1600 extents unflagged, nvme_iops stable. attach queue dropped by ~45%.

ops-bot: [metric] us-west1 nvme_iops=7200 attach_queue=12 -> 6 after batch1

josh: good. what's the estimated time to finish all?

maria: at batch=200 + 250ms sleep, rough ETA ~18m for full set.

nora-support: sending a short update to customers: "We've mitigated a transient cleaner regression in us-west1 and GPU attach latency is improving. We'll post a follow-up once all background work completes."

samir: long-term we need a safer guardrail: cleaner dry-run mode must not flip persistent flags, and config changes should be canaryed per 10 nodes first. also add a preflight that compares flagged delta to expected thresholds.

josh: +1. also we should add a consumer-side fallback so scheduler can use pre-warmed scratch volumes rather than forcing attach when ephemeral pool is under pressure. reduces customer impact.

maria: filing a postmortem ticket now with remediation steps and cost analysis. quick note: cost tradeoff here — immediate replacement of impacted instances (~30 nodes) would restore capacity faster but costs ~+$4.7k in reserved/spot churn. the unpreserve route is slower but negligible cost.

tess: add to postmortem: kernel patch ID, config diff, who approved, and test coverage gap. also include the `rvctl` commands we ran and the exact ops-bot alerts.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollback not required. manual config override applied by maria at 2026-03-23T10:50Z.

maria: thanks all. monitoring for the next 1h, will reopen if anything regresses. :coffee:
